page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 16 physical cores and a single thread per core. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB per core. Graphics and parallel processing workloads are accelerated by two NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a combined 48 GB of VRAM. This instance does not include local storage, and comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier performance in single-core metrics, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance is strong, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is also strong, though small-block cached read bandwidth remains average. The dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs deliver top-tier LLM inference speeds, processing prompts and generating text in the top 10% for both small (135M) and medium (7B) models.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers high qualitative cost efficiency for GPU-accelerated tasks by pairing a high-capacity 192 GB memory footprint with dual energy-efficient L4 accelerators. However, the lack of local storage requires external storage solutions, which may introduce latency or additional configuration overhead. The shared CPU allocation is another tradeoff to consider for sustained, non-GPU compute-bound tasks. This server is highly suited for machine learning inference, image processing, data science pipelines, and medium-scale LLM deployments.
